findings.title: App modules are still all imported eagerly
findings.body: Each `import("./...")` expression is evaluated while constructing `appStore`, so importing this module immediately starts loading every app package. This does not defer loading until a selected integration is used, and unused import promises can reject without any consumer. Store loader functions (for example, `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) and invoke only the selected loader at call sites to actually make integrations lazy.

findings.title: Recurring calendar deletions are no longer included in the awaited cleanup
findings.body: The async `forEach` callback awaits `getCalendar` before it pushes a deletion into `apiDeletes`, but `forEach` does not await its callbacks. The handler subsequently proceeds to delete booking records, send notifications, and eventually calls `Promise.all(apiDeletes)` while that array can still be empty. Consequently recurring cancellation can return successfully without deleting remote calendar events; rejected imports/deletions also become unhandled rejections. Build and await the work explicitly, e.g. with `await Promise.all(credentials.map(async credential => ...))`, rather than mutating `apiDeletes` from detached callbacks.

findings.title: Calendar cleanup errors escape the surrounding try block
findings.body: Changing this callback to `async` makes `getCalendar` asynchronous, but `forEach` neither waits for the callback nor propagates its rejection to the enclosing `try/catch`. The reschedule flow can send the reschedule email and return success before calendar/video deletion has started or completed, and a failed dynamic import or deletion is unhandled rather than logged. Collect these operations and `await Promise.all(...)` inside the try block.

findings.title: Reschedule mutation returns before dynamically loaded integrations are deleted
findings.body: The async callback passed to `forEach` is detached. Since it now awaits the app import before calling `deleteEvent`, the mutation marks the booking cancelled and sends email/webhooks before cleanup is performed, and failures while loading or deleting an integration are unhandled. Replace the `forEach(async ...)` with awaited promises so cancellation is either completed or its failure is handled before the mutation finishes.
